items.addition: This is a walkthrough of how we built the shell of this home addition, step by step. Day one, we come out and mark the exact footprint, so the new room sits inside your property lines and the city's setbacks. Next, the footings. That's the foundation of the addition. It shows you the real size of the new space, and it's what holds up the whole structure. Here's how it comes together. Steel goes into the footing, with dowels bent up out of the concrete. Then the first rows of block go up over them. Inside, the soil is filled in, packed tight, and treated to help keep termites away. A plastic vapor barrier goes on top, to help keep moisture from coming up through your slab. Then the slab is poured, locking into the block walls. From there, the walls keep going up. Steel bars overlap the dowels and run up inside the block, and those cells get filled with concrete, all the way to the tie beam. That's what makes it one complete structure. On top, we form and pour the tie beam. It locks the walls together and connects the structure to your roof trusses. Its height is very important. It usually has to match the existing house, and it has to work with your truss design. Then the trusses go up, and each one gets hurricane straps, to help keep the wind from lifting your roof. Block, steel, tie beam and straps, all working together. This addition isn't finished yet. Follow along to see what comes next. Planning an addition in South Florida? Let's build it right.
